project.title: Predicting GDP per Capita Using Feature Engineering
project.objective: Build a machine learning model to predict a country's GDP per capita based on macroeconomic and socioeconomic indicators, following a complete data science pipeline from raw data inspection to model evaluation.
project.note: No dataset is provided. Either collect one from public sources (World Bank Open Data, IMF WEO, OECD.Stat, Our World in Data) or create a synthetic CSV matching the schema below, then apply the pipeline in order.
project.rationale: Real-world economic datasets rarely arrive clean. Numeric indicators are commonly stored as text with units and symbols (e.g., '$ 21,430', '3.2 %', '68.5 years'), and macro panels frequently contain sentinel strings like 'Not Available' or '..' for missing observations. This mirrors real-world data imperfection and motivates systematic feature extraction.

columns.name: region
columns.description: Geographic region (Europe & Central Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa, East Asia & Pacific, etc.)

columns.name: internet_penetration
columns.description: Share of population using the internet (text, e.g., '88.7 %')

columns.name: gov_spending_gdp_share
columns.description: Government expenditure as % of GDP (text, e.g., '44.1 %')

columns.name: trade_openness_index
columns.description: Trade openness index (numeric already, or text with units)

columns.name: currency_regime
columns.description: Exchange rate regime (Floating, Fixed, Pegged, Currency Union)

columns.name: income_group
columns.description: World Bank income classification (Low, Lower-Middle, Upper-Middle, High)

columns.name: democracy_index
columns.description: Democracy index score (text with artifacts, e.g., '8.53 pts', 'Not Available')

columns.name: gdp_per_capita
columns.description: GDP per capita in USD (TARGET, text, e.g., '$ 51,204')

dataset_schema.notes: Several numeric columns are object-typed. The country and region columns have high cardinality; income_group and currency_regime have low cardinality. 'population' mixes magnitudes (million/billion) and requires unit-aware parsing, unlike the laptop project's single-unit columns.

economics_fundamentals: Definition and components of GDP; difference between GDP total, GDP per capita, and GDP growth
Purchasing power parity (PPP) vs. nominal exchange-rate conversion; why PPP-adjusted figures are preferred for cross-country comparison

Relationships explored in EDA: Solow-style associations between investment/productivity and income, Okun's law intuition (unemployment vs. output), human capital proxies (literacy, life expectancy) and development levels
Structural features of economies: export dependence, government spending share, resource curse hypothesis, income classification systems
Right-skew of income/GDP distributions (a few very rich countries, many middle- and low-income ones) and implications for regression metrics
data_science_fundamentals: String parsing and unit stripping with .str.replace and .str.extract
Magnitude rescaling ('million'/'billion' multipliers) as an extension of simple unit stripping
Missing data strategies: sentinel encoding ('Not Available' -> 0 or NaN) and its trade-offs
Feature engineering: composites (e.g., exports per capita), keeping dimensionality low
Correlation analysis and multicollinearity among macro aggregates (many indicators co-move with development level)
Categorical encoding: one-hot for low cardinality, target (mean) encoding for high cardinality
Target leakage: computing encodings on the full dataset before splitting inflates test scores
Train/test splitting with fixed random_state for reproducibility
Decision trees and Random Forests: bagging, feature subsampling, robustness to non-linearities
Evaluation metrics: MAE (interpretable in USD), RMSE (outlier-sensitive), R-squared (variance explained)
Feature importance: impurity-based bias toward high-cardinality encoded features; permutation importance as debiased alternative

pipeline_tasks.title: Data Loading and Initial Inspection
pipeline_tasks.task: Load and inspect the macroeconomic dataset:
steps: Import the pandas library as pd
Load the dataset 'macro_indicators.csv' into a DataFrame named df
Print the first 5 rows of the DataFrame using .head()
Inspect the data types and non-null counts by calling .info() on df
Check df.columns for naming inconsistencies
Scan for sentinel values ('Not Available', '..', 'No data')

pipeline_tasks.title: Extracting Percentage-Based Economic Indicators
pipeline_tasks.task: Parse percentage indicators stored as text:
steps: Iterate over the columns ['unemployment_rate', 'inflation_rate', 'literacy_rate', 'internet_penetration', 'exports_gdp_share', 'gov_spending_gdp_share'] using a for loop
For each column, remove the string ' %' using .str.replace(' %', ''), then also strip any ',' thousands separator, and convert the result to float using .astype(float)
Verify with df[list_of_columns].head() and df[...].describe()

pipeline_tasks.title: Cleaning Population, Life Expectancy and Other Text Columns
pipeline_tasks.task: Extract numeric data from the remaining string-based columns, casting each to string first for idempotency:
steps: Clean population: .astype(str), replace ' million' with '' and multiply by 1e6 OR use a mapping {'million': 1e6, 'billion': 1e9}; handle rows with plain numbers; convert to float. Alternative: parse with a regex extracting number and unit, then compute the scaled value
Clean life_expectancy: .astype(str), replace ' years' with '', convert to float
Clean democracy_index: .astype(str), replace 'Not Available' with '0', replace ' pts' with '', convert to float
Confirm no ValueError from unexpected strings using .unique() checks

pipeline_tasks.title: Feature Engineering for Economic Structure
steps: Create 'exports_intensity' interaction: exports_gdp_share * trade_openness_index (composite intensity measure)
Create 'digital_readiness' = internet_penetration * literacy_rate / 100 (interaction of human and digital capital)
Drop intermediate columns that are fully represented by the new features
Document each transformation

pipeline_tasks.title: Exploratory Data Analysis for GDP Drivers
pipeline_tasks.task: Perform EDA using Seaborn and Matplotlib:
steps: Create numeric_df using df.select_dtypes(include='number')
Create a correlation heatmap with sns.heatmap(numeric_df.corr(), annot=True, cmap='coolwarm')
Identify features with the highest absolute correlation with 'gdp_per_capita'
Boxplot: income_group on x-axis vs gdp_per_capita on y-axis
Boxplot: unemployment_rate (rounded to integer bins) on x-axis vs gdp_per_capita on y-axis
Note: expect strong right skew; consider a log transform of the target for diagnostics (log(gdp_per_capita))

pipeline_tasks.title: Encoding Categorical Variables and Splitting Data
pipeline_tasks.task: Encode categorical features and perform a train/test split:
steps: Identify categorical columns using df.select_dtypes(include=['object']).columns
For each column: if fewer than 5 unique values, one-hot encode with pd.get_dummies(..., drop_first=True); otherwise target encode with .map(df.groupby(col)['gdp_per_capita'].mean())

Expected behavior: 'currency_regime' and 'resource_dependent' fall below the threshold; 'region' and 'country' exceed it (note: target-encoding 'country' is borderline circular for this target - prefer dropping 'country' or using frequency encoding, and discuss why)
Define X as all columns except 'gdp_per_capita', and y as 'gdp_per_capita'
Split into X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test with an 80/20 split and random_state=42
Recommended stretch: fit target encoders on the training set only and fill unseen test categories with the training mean

pipeline_tasks.title: Building the Random Forest Regressor
pipeline_tasks.task: Initialize and train the regression model:
steps: Import RandomForestRegressor from sklearn.ensemble
Initialize the model as rf_model with random_state=42
Fit the model using X_train and y_train
Generate predictions on X_test and store them in y_pred

pipeline_tasks.title: Evaluating Model Performance and Feature Importance
pipeline_tasks.task: Evaluate the model and visualize feature importances:
steps: Import mean_absolute_error and r2_score from sklearn.metrics
Compute both metrics using y_test and y_pred and print the results
Extract feature importances from rf_model.feature_importances_
Identify the top 5 most important features using np.argsort()
Plot them with a horizontal sns.barplot()
Interpret: do life expectancy, internet penetration, or export intensity dominate? Compare against economic intuition

phase_1_problem_understanding: Define the continuous target (GDP per capita, household income, inflation, consumption, wages)
Choose stakeholder-relevant metrics (currency units, percentage points)
Ground expectations in domain theory before looking at data
phase_2_data_audit: Source from reputable providers (World Bank, IMF, OECD) or document synthetic generation
Audit dtypes: expected vs. actual per column
Identify sentinel values and disguised missing data
phase_3_feature_engineering: Impute vs sentinel vs drop - justify per column
Build theory-motivated composites (ratios, per-capita intensities, interaction indices)
phase_4_eda: Examine target skew; consider log transformation
Boxplots of discrete/grouped features vs target
phase_5_encoding_and_splitting: Split categorical columns by cardinality threshold (~5)
One-hot low cardinality; target/frequency encode high cardinality, fitted on train only
phase_6_modeling: Baseline: mean predictor or linear regression
Compare train vs test metrics for over/underfitting diagnosis
phase_7_evaluation: Report MAE, RMSE, and R-squared together
Plot predicted vs actual; examine residuals by region/income group
phase_8_iteration_communication: Hyperparameter tuning with GridSearchCV or RandomizedSearchCV
Cross-validation (k-fold, ideally grouped by region or year for panel data)
Compare Gradient Boosting / XGBoost against Random Forest
Translate findings into policy-relevant language for non-technical readers

common_pitfalls_checklist: Target leakage: target encoding or scaling fitted on the full dataset before splitting
Leaky identifiers: encoding 'country' names with target means when the target is a per-country statistic
Non-idempotent cleaning: rerunning cells crashes on already-numeric columns
Mixed magnitudes in text ('million' vs 'billion' vs raw numbers) breaking .astype(float)
Decimal comma vs decimal point conventions in European-format data
Comparing nominal GDP across countries without acknowledging PPP and exchange-rate distortion
Outlier dominance: a handful of microstates or oil economies distorting RMSE and impurity importances
Ignoring temporal structure: cross-sectional rules differ from panel/time-series splits (data snooping across years)
Treating suspiciously high R-squared as success rather than a leakage warning

extensions_after_modeling: Log-transform the target and compare MAE/R2 against the raw-scale model
Add a second model family (GradientBoostingRegressor) and benchmark
If the data includes multiple years, add year as a feature or use grouped cross-validation by year
SHAP values for per-country explanation of predictions
